title: Square array of cylinders: Darcy permeability (analytic)
description:
Steady Stokes flow through a square array of solid cylinders: one periodic cell (l = 128 um, periodic x and y) with a centred solid disc of radius a (a material without viscosity: no-slip halfway bounce-back on its staircased boundary; relaxation_time 2: the steady TRT result with halfway bounce-back does not depend on it, and the march needs ~3x fewer lattice steps than at 1, lattice Mach ~5e-3), the liquid driven by a uniform body force f along x (body_force; solid cells ignore it). The sweep runs a over 12..32 um (solid fraction c = pi a^2 / l^2 = 0.028..0.196).
Analytic (Sangani & Acrivos 1982 / Drummond & Tahir 1984, square array, Stokes): K = l^2 (-ln c - 1.476 + 2 c - 1.774 c^2 + 4.076 c^3) / (8 pi), Darcy U_sup = K f / mu, U_sup the superficial velocity (mean over the whole cell, solid included). A body force on the liquid alone is the same Stokes problem as a mean pressure gradient G = f (the force per cylinder G l^2 then includes the mean-gradient pressure on the solid), so no (1 - c) factor appears.
Derived values tab: K_sim = mean(u_x) mu / f over the cell vs K_ref (tolerance 6 %: the staircased disc shifts the effective radius by a fraction of a cell, worst at a = 12 cells; the c^3 series is good to ~1 % at c = 0.2; Reynolds <= 0.2).
Sweep tab: K_sim versus a with the dashed K_vs_radius.

parameters.name: mu_f
parameters.description: dynamic viscosity of the liquid in Pa s

parameters.name: l_cell
parameters.description: side of the periodic unit cell (cylinder spacing)

parameters.name: f_x
parameters.description: body force density on the liquid along x in N/m^3 (the equivalent mean pressure gradient)

parameters.name: K_ref
parameters.description: Darcy permeability of the square array in m^2

parameters.name: U_sup_ref
parameters.description: superficial velocity in m/s (1.4e-3 at a = 12 um, 3.3e-4 at 32 um)
